Yup, this is a trouble with render targets, they are flipped compared to image based textures.

Now everything else in the lib is made to look ok with images, which means render targets look wrong (even while these are the ones which are technically correct).

One possible workaround is to flip UVs for objects which use such generated textures.

Yep, as I mention [here](http://stackoverflow.com/a/11332554/1137134) this is a long standing issue we haven't been able to nail nicely yet.

As far as I understand, the problem is that `UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL` didn't seem to be well supported back when we were trying to implement this, so sometimes loaded textures weren't being flipped. So the solution was to invert the V in all the geometries.

I don't know how's the support nowadays, but would be good to remove this hack eventually.
@mrdoob I think `UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL` works on images but not on render targets.

> @mrdoob I think `UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL` works on images but not on render targets.

But render target won't need it, right? That's why it's now being flipped because the UVs are flipped but the render target is not.
Yup, it just means you can't use this flag to work around current flipping (or if everything was already fixed and for some reason you indeed wanted flipped render target).
The Three.js Rapid Response Team is truly awesome. :-)
@alteredq do you remember what was the issue with `UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL`? was it lack of support?

> @alteredq do you remember what was the issue with UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL? was it lack of support?

It was simply not existing when we were starting doing these things, it got added to specs only later on ;)

Otherwise, it should work, just we are already too deep with these UV flipping hacks everywhere :S.
Ah I see. I'll give it a go at some point then.

From few times I tried to fix these flips it always ended up in whack-a-mole - fix one thing, go through all examples, have something else getting broken, repeat.

It should be possible but it needs a lot of patience. If you'll go for it, let me know if it would become too much, I can give a hand with something.
